title: Multiband ALMA polarimetry of the jet base and kiloparsec-scale jet of 3C 273: A multicomponent Faraday structure in the nucleus
question: Determine the polarization and Faraday rotation structure of the nucleus (multiple polarized components versus internal Faraday rotation) and the magnetic field structure of the kiloparsec-scale jet in the quasar 3C 273 using multiband ALMA polarimetry.

data.sensitivity: Theoretical continuum sensitivity: 0.16 mJy (Band 4), 0.44 mJy (Band 6), 0.14 mJy (Band 7 Nov 15), 0.075 mJy (Band 7 Nov 23)

what.value: EVPA measurements in band 6 from April 2017 EHT campaign and earlier ALMA observations

evidence.quote: Figure 8 shows the EVPA measurements from and this paper along with the data from (cite: goddi21) that were taken during the EHT campaign in April 2017.

what.value: Black hole mass estimate M_BH = 10^9.1 M_sun

evidence.loc: Polarization and Faraday rotation in the core
evidence.quote: Adopting the latest black hole mass estimate for 3C 273, $M_\mathrm{BH} = 10^{9.1}$ M$_\odot$ by (cite: li22) gives us the scale $r_g = 6\times10^{-5}$ pc.

what.value: Jet magnetic field strength (~2 G at <=0.06 mas and >=6 G) and thermal electron density (6 x 10^-2 cm^-3)

evidence.loc: Polarization and Faraday rotation in the core
evidence.quote: From VLBI studies of 3C 273 up to 86 GHz (cite: attridge05), we can consider a jet magnetic field strength of at least 6 G (cite: savolainen2008) and jet size of order 1 pc at these frequencies.

evidence.loc: Polarization and Faraday rotation in the core
evidence.quote: Along with a thermal electron density of $6\times10^{-2}$ cm$^{-3}$ (cite: roeser00), these parameters can provide mean RMs and dispersions of order $10^5$ rad m$^{-2}$ that can readily account for the high-RM component properties.

recipe.method: Standard ALMA calibration and polarization calibration using 3C 279, with Spw-independent polarization modeling and self-bandpass calibration in Band 6, D-term copying from Nov 23 to Nov 15 in Band 7, and two rounds of phase-only and amplitude+phase self-calibration using 3C 273.
key_parameters: Phase-only self-cal solint = int; phase and amplitude self-cal solint = 10 s (Bands 4 and 6) and 30 s (Band 7)
assumptions: Stokes V vanishes at 232.86 GHz for Band 6 self-bandpass model (I = 4.35 Jy, alpha = -0.85, Q = 0.0238 Jy, U = -0.1212 Jy); similar D-terms between Nov 15 and Nov 23 in Band 7

recipe.goal: Extract channel-wise Stokes parameters and uncertainties of the nucleus
recipe.method: Fit visibility data with a delta component at the phase center in each 31.25 MHz channel independently using UVMULTIFIT, and run 1000 Monte Carlo simulations to propagate thermal and systematic calibration uncertainties; fit power-law spectral index to total intensity.
key_parameters: 1000 Monte Carlo realizations; noise std devs: X-Y Phase = 2 deg, X-Y Bandpass amp = 0.1% (B4, B6) / 0.2% (B7), X-Y Bandpass phase = 0.5 deg, D-terms = 0.5% (B4, B7 Nov 23) / 2% (B6) / 1% (B7 Nov 15)
assumptions: Single point source dominates emission at phase center

recipe.goal: Model wavelength-dependent core polarization via QU-fitting
recipe.method: Fit complex fractional polarization p(lambda^2) = q(lambda^2) + i u(lambda^2) across Bands 4, 6, and 7 (Nov 15) against four parametric Faraday rotation models (S, T_inv, S2, T2) using a nested-sampling backend.
key_parameters: Four models: S (3 params), T_inv (5 params), S2 (6 params), T2 (8 params)
assumptions: External Faraday dispersion or thin screens parameterized by mean RM, dispersion sigma_RM, intrinsic fractional polarization p_0, and intrinsic angle psi_0

recipe.goal: Image kiloparsec-scale jet polarization and map spectral index
recipe.method: Image aggregated bandwidth and individual Spws with tclean, extract Stokes I, Q, U with immath, compute fractional polarization and EVPA along ridge lines and transverse slices, smooth single-Spw images to common beam with imsmooth, align using QA2 images, and fit pixel-by-pixel power-law spectral index across 12 Spws.
key_parameters: Polarization cutoff: I > 5*rms and polarized flux > 3*rms; Spectral index cutoff: I > 3*rms in each Spw, 10% calibration uncertainty added in quadrature, accepted fits with chi^2 < 18.307 (95% confidence for 10 dof); common beam 0.54'' x 0.44''; Band 6 declination shift -0.043''
assumptions: Power-law spectrum I proportional to nu^+alpha across 138-350 GHz

answer_key.quantity: Core spectral index (alpha_core, using Nov 15 Band 7)

evidence.loc: Extracting Stokes parameters of the nucleus
evidence.quote: The emission over all the bands is optically thin with a spectral index of $\alpha_{\rm core}=-0.7915\pm0.0003$ and a reduced $\chi^2=2.76$ of the fit when using the 15 November epoch in band 7.

evidence.loc: Extracting Stokes parameters of the nucleus
evidence.quote: If we use the 23 November epoch instead, the spectral index would be $-0.905\pm0.002$ with a significantly higher reduced $\chi^2=123.0$, further supporting our decision to use only the 15 November epoch in the modeling of the core polarization.

answer_key.quantity: Core T2 model intrinsic polarization fraction 1 (p_1)
Core T2 model intrinsic polarization fraction 2 (p_2)
Core T2 model intrinsic polarization angle 1 (psi_0,1)
Core T2 model intrinsic polarization angle 2 (psi_0,2)
Nominal single-band RM in Band 6 (linear fit)

evidence.quote: Our new data taken over 1.5 years later show very different behavior with a nearly flat polarization angle over the 1.3 mm band, resulting in a much smaller nominal RM of $\sim-8.4\times10^4$ rad m$^−2$ if a simple linear fit as shown in Fig. 8 is performed.
In all the ALMA bands the brightest hotspot H2 where our images are centered is highly polarized with a fractional polarization of 20-30%.

answer_key.quantity: Kiloparsec-scale jet ridge spectral index (138-350 GHz)

evidence.loc: Polarization and spectral index of the kiloparsec-scale jet
evidence.quote: The spectral index distribution is relatively steep, around $-0.9$, but several flatter portions of $-0.8$ are seen along the ridge.

not_stated_but_needed: Weighting scheme and Briggs robust parameter used in tclean
Image size and pixel cell sizes for Bands 4 and 7
Stopping threshold and masking strategy in tclean
Primary beam correction status for the kiloparsec-scale jet images (especially for spectral index mapping across bands)
Specific nested-sampling software package, number of live points, and prior distributions used for the QU-fitting
missing_for_reproduction: Prior bounds and specific nested sampling algorithm/package used for QU-fitting
Custom Monte Carlo CASA script used to perturb calibration tables and compute parallactic angle
Exact tclean weighting (e.g., Briggs robust parameter), cell sizes for Bands 4 and 7, and stopping criteria
score_reason: High reproducibility: raw ALMA data are public, the intermediate channel-by-channel Stokes table (poldata.dat) and FITS images are deposited at CDS, the calibration overrides (flux scales, self-cal intervals, Band 6 self-bandpass model, MC noise amplitudes) and QU-fitting analytic equations are explicitly given. Minor deductions for omitting the nested-sampling priors/software name and tclean weighting parameters.
rediscovery_reason: Both raw ALMA visibilities (2018.1.00357.S) and the intermediate extracted core polarization spectrum (poldata.dat at CDS) are public, and the main results are exact numeric Bayesian QU-fitting parameters (RM, sigma_RM, p_0, psi_0, ln Z) and core spectral index.
